title: Redwood POC Weekly Sync - Benchmark Review vs Baseline Provider
summary: Weekly POC sync to review benchmark results (latency & throughput) for Redwood vs customer's baseline provider. Discussed tuning knobs (batching, KV cache, quantization), alignment of test configs, network egress variability, and next steps for a controlled perf run. Action items assigned for data and security checks and a follow-up benchmark with pinned model/sequence lengths.
next_steps: Redwood to run controlled perf run with pinned seq lengths and share results (Evan) by 2026-09-03
FluxBank to provide production-like request logs and 1k representative prompts by 2026-09-02
Security to review audit log sample and share comments (Sara) by 2026-09-04
Schedule 1-hour deep-dive for canary/rollout plan if perf looks good (Maya to coordinate)
action_items: Maya Chen: schedule follow-up deep-dive and send calendar invite by 2026-09-02
Evan Liu: run controlled perf run (pinned seq lengths 32/128/512) and upload results + graphs by 2026-09-03
Liam O'Connor: share request distribution and 1k prompt sample by 2026-09-02
Sara Ng: share SOC2 artifact location and KMS questions in thread by 2026-09-04
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: All right everyone, thanks for joining, um it's Maya from Redwood, I'm here with Evan and Sofia. How's everyone?
[00:06] Jason Kramer: Hey Maya, yeah good thanks, Jason here. We got Priya and Liam on as well.
[00:10] Priya Desai: hi sorry late, had a quick deploy hiccup.
[00:13] Evan Liu: no worries, we'll keep it tight. Today's agenda — quick recaps of the baseline numbers you shared, then go over Redwood's weekly run, highlight gaps, and agree next steps.
[00:25] Liam O'Connor: sounds good, we've been eager to see the delta on p99 latency and the tokens/sec.
[00:30] Maya Chen: perfect. Jason, quick check — same baseline provider we're comparing to is your current managed endpoint on GCP Vertex with n1-standard fronting and T4s behind, right?
[00:40] Jason Kramer: yeah, that's right. Small correction — it's our sharded setup on Vertex with autoscale, the baseline spreadsheet is in the drive link you have.
[00:47] Evan Liu: okay pulling up the Redwood run from last night — link in chat. You'll see median latency is about 38ms shorter for the 32-seq runs, throughput is roughly 1.8x for tokens/sec compared to the baseline. But p99 is closer, like 12-18ms improvement, so it's smaller.
[01:05] Priya Desai: are those numbers with batching enabled? we had seen our baseline with a 64-batch config.
[01:11] Evan Liu: good question. Redwood run used dynamic continuous batching with a target max batch of 32, and we had KV cache warm for the prefix set. Baseline's 64-batch might boost throughput but hurts tail latency, which matches what you reported.
[01:22] Jason Kramer: right, our ops team tunes for throughput during off-hours so our p50 looks great but p99 spikes. We're trying to understand the tradeoff.
[01:29] Maya Chen: yeah that's a classic tradeoff. For POC we usually run both pinned batch and dynamic to show the profile. Evan, can you call out memory footprint and GPU utilization?
[01:36] Evan Liu: sure — on the Redwood node GPU utilization hovered 72-85% during 512-seq runs, memory stayed under 78% thanks to our quant quantization path (transcription: quantizashun), and with int8 profiles we shave about 20% memory, which lets us keep throughput up without OOMs.
[01:55] Liam O'Connor: int8 results looked promising — any accuracy/regression monitoring tied to that?
[02:00] Evan Liu: we ran a quick eval suite — small token-level diffs in some completions but no major quality regressions on your exemplar prompts. We flagged 3 cases in the spreadsheet under notes.
[02:12] Priya Desai: curious about network egress — our baseline is in the same region but we still see variability, could that be skewing p99?
[02:18] Evan Liu: yes network jitter and instance spin-ups on the baseline autoscaler can add tail noise. On Redwood's Dedicated run we saw more stable tail since instances are pinned for the test. We did note one spike correlated with a background snapshot on the node though.
[02:32] Jason Kramer: can you run a controlled perf test with no autoscaling on both sides? that's what we'd like to see to remove the noise.
[02:38] Maya Chen: absolutely — that's one of the next steps. Evan will run a pinned-config test with seq lengths 32/128/512 and also match the batch size to your baseline.
[02:46] Evan Liu: yes, and we'll also push a run with prefix caching disabled to show worst-case cold start numbers.
[02:52] Sara Ng: quick security question — where are audit logs stored for this POC and how granular are they?
[02:57] Sofia Martinez: we keep request-level metadata in the private audit logs; we can provide a sample export. For private deployments we integrate with KMS and HSM — I put the SOC2 references in the notes link.
[03:10] Sara Ng: perfect, please include retention periods.
[03:13] Sofia Martinez: will do.
[03:15] Priya Desai: back to throughput — what about batching latency curve? do you have a plot?
[03:20] Evan Liu: yes spreadsheet has latency vs batch size plots. For 64 batch you get 2.3x tokens/sec but p99 increases nonlinearly. For many of your interactive workflows we think batch 16-32 is sweet spot.
[03:33] Liam O'Connor: are you doing any kernel-level optimizations or is it standard cudnn?
[03:36] Evan Liu: we have kernel selection and attention kernels optimized — sometimes the profiler shows we hit a custom fused kernel on sequence 128 which gives wins. Also our runtime chooses kernels based on seq distribution, so if you have many short sequences we automatically route to the low-latency path.
[03:52] Jason Kramer: interesting. Could you also provide a byte-level cost calc? our finance folks care about $/1M tokens per day.
[03:59] Maya Chen: yes we'll add a cost normalized sheet — cost per million tokens at current commit levels, and also cost delta vs baseline for the same throughput target.
[04:08] Priya Desai: minor note, the transcription in your sheet had qv cache spelled as "K-V cash" which confused our legal team.
[04:14] Maya Chen: ha, apologies for the auto-transcript. We'll clean labels in the sheet.
[04:18] Evan Liu: one more data point — when we enable prefix/KV caching with the representative prompt set you gave us, we saw median token latency drop another 10-12ms on average, because repeated context avoids recompute.
[04:30] Priya Desai: that was with a warmed KV cache across requests? how many warm sessions did you simulate?
[04:34] Evan Liu: we ran a warm scenario with 500 unique session prefixes and a cold run for baseline. Warm cache results are in tab 'cache-warm'.
[04:42] Jason Kramer: I'm concerned about stability over longer runs — can you run a 12-hour soak?
[04:47] Maya Chen: yes we can spin up a soak test, but given POC time constraints we usually do a 2-3 hour sustained run plus a longer overnight soak if needed. Do you want us to schedule the 12-hour?
[04:58] Jason Kramer: let's do a 6-hour soak first, if that passes we'll extend.
[05:02] Maya Chen: noted — Evan will kick off a 6-hour soak after the controlled perf run.
[05:07] Liam O'Connor: about the baseline, we noticed the baseline had intermittent CPU throttling on the host, probably because of noisy neighbor VM scheduling — did you control for host type in your comparisons?
[05:18] Evan Liu: good call — we matched GPU type (T4 equivalent) but not host CPU. For the controlled run we'll pin host shapes to remove that variable.
[05:26] Priya Desai: any pointer on quantization artifacts? we saw some hallucinations increase in a couple of templates.
[05:31] Evan Liu: the int8 path can introduce tiny distributional changes. We'll flag those prompts and run ablation with int8 vs fp16 and produce a delta report.
[05:40] Jason Kramer: and SLA expectations — if we go Dedicated what's typical SLO for p99?
[05:45] Maya Chen: for dedicated we target 99th latency SLOs per model and route policy; typical SLO we aim for is p99 under Xms for interactive models but we customize per customer. We'll send a draft SLA page.
[05:56] Sara Ng: please include RBAC and SSO details too.
[05:59] Sofia Martinez: yes, RBAC + SAML SSO are in our enterprise pack, will share doc.
[06:04] Priya Desai: another small question — how do you handle eviction/auto-scaling warmups on Dedicated?
[06:10] Evan Liu: Dedicated gives you pinning and configured burst capacity; you can choose to keep a minimal pool warm and allow burst nodes for spikes, and we have a warmup policy to prefetch KV cache for known sessions.
[06:22] Jason Kramer: good. One last technical ask — can you instrument traces for a single request end-to-end including network, encode, attention, kernel time, decode?
[06:31] Evan Liu: yes we have per-token trace hooks and will provide a sample trace for a 128-seq request. Note traces may include internal kernel names which we can redact.
[06:40] Maya Chen: OK wrapping up — action items we captured, Evan runs pinned perf + 6-hour soak, Liam and Priya provide logs and prompts, Sara will look at security artifacts, Maya will schedule deep-dive. Anything else?
[06:52] Jason Kramer: no that's it, thanks everyone.
[06:55] Maya Chen: thanks all, talk soon.
